transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose what brings me in is I’ve been avoiding certain things more than I’d like to admit. It’s not anything dramatic, I don’t want to make too much of it, but I keep steering clear of my workshop, and I tend to skip family get-togethers if there’s a chance my brother-in-law will be there.

After all this time, I’m just… tired of planning my life around not running into those reminders, if that makes sense.
Can you tell me more about why you avoid your workshop and family gatherings where your brother-in-law might be present?

Well… it’s mostly that those places bring things back up, if that makes sense. My workshop used to be somewhere I’d go to keep busy, but now I find myself making excuses not to go in there.

And with family gatherings, if I hear my brother-in-law might be there, I’ll usually decide I’m tired or that I’ve got something else to do. I don’t mean to make it sound like some big dramatic thing… I just don’t want to run into those reminders. After all these years, though, I’m getting tired of arranging myself around it.
Can you tell me more about what comes up for you in those moments—like, what thoughts or memories tend to surface when you're near those reminders?

Well… it’s not constant or anything, I don’t want to overstate it. But sometimes, out of nowhere, I’ll sort of see his hand again… with that heavy tool in it. Like a picture that just pops into my head.

It can happen at odd times, too—like when I’m shaving, or if I’m trying to work on a painting. And then my chest tightens up before I even really have time to think about it. I know that probably sounds strange, but that’s the main thing that comes up.

latest_inference.note: The patient described intrusive, trauma-related memories (e.g., seeing 'his hand again... with that heavy tool in it') and physiological reactivity (e.g., chest tightening) when exposed to reminders. This presentation, along with avoidance behavior, is most consistent with PTSD (F43.10). Other anxiety and obsessive-compulsive disorders have been ruled out due to the specific trauma-related nature of the symptoms.
